issues.description: The problem statement specifies a SealSaloon constructor that takes a String parameter (SealSaloon(String)) and explicitly states the constructor takes the saloon name as a String. However, the provided template usage (Main.java) and the solution implementation (SealSaloon.java) use / provide a no-argument constructor (new SealSaloon() and public SealSaloon()). This mismatch between the specification and code examples/solution can confuse students about the required constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across all artifacts. Either update the problem statement to require a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()) or update the template and solution to provide a constructor with a String parameter (SealSaloon(String name)). A minimal non-breaking fix is to add an overloaded constructor SealSaloon(String name) in SealSaloon that delegates to the existing no-arg constructor (or stores the name) and update example usages in Main to pass a saloon name if the problem statement is kept as-is.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) specifies a constructor SealSaloon(String) (a saloon name parameter) but the provided codebase (template usage and solution implementation) uses a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). This mismatch of the constructor signature for the same conceptual entity (the SealSaloon constructor that accepts a name) can confuse students about which constructor to implement and how the saloon name should be stored/accessed.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across artifacts. Either update the solution and template to provide a public SealSaloon(String name) constructor (and add a private name field with a getter) to match the problem statement, or revise the problem statement to require a no-argument SealSaloon() constructor. Preferably implement public SealSaloon(String name) in src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java and update Main.java examples accordingly.
